Anateur interest in the farth sciences in the form of rockhounding dates for back in the history of man, but it was not until the 1920s in the western United States that there was sufficient popular interest to form clubs. Now there are over 1000 listed club, in the 50 states devoted almost entirely to the recommational, educational and scientific pursuits in connection with the hobby.
Today approximately 19,5 of the population lives in the western half of the U.S. and Alaska. However, most of the rockhounds, 59%, are located in the west. This ratio is no coincidence since the open public domain lands are in the west, with geological resources accessible to the hobbiest.
A survey of 881 people questioned in field areas in the western states during 1965 - 1967 showed that 6.6% of the total were visitors from the east, midwest and southern parts of the nation. Tourism of this type is expected to increase dramatically as one people join this wholesome activity in which all members of the family participate. Thus restriction on the use of public lands will have an increased effect upon people throughout the entire nation. A recent industry survey concluded that approximately two million people comprize the rockhound market in the United etates. This is substantially more than the quarter million people who regularly visit field areas in search of resource materials; however, this larger market can be maintained only by the antibusiosm and frequency of those who en age in the field press of the hobby.
